purpose: A MEANING check, not a numeric one. Every other gate in this repo compares
our vectors against a reference implementation and asks whether the numbers
agree. This one asks whether the vectors mean anything, and it answers with
ORDER rather than with decimals: sentences about the same thing must come
out closer than sentences about different things. No tolerance, no epsilon.
Why that gap is worth its own file: a reference comparison passes when both
sides are wrong the SAME way. tools/verify_embed_e2e.py prepends the same
task prefix to the reference that the runtime applies, so a wrongly-chosen
prompt agrees with itself; and a container whose arch was read wrong returns
vectors that are correctly shaped, correctly normed and deterministic. This
corpus needs no reference at all -- which is also why the checker is stdlib
only and runs against a cold dist zip with nothing installed.
design: TWELVE clusters of THREE sentences, chosen so the twelve topics are mutually
unrelated -- no two clusters share a domain, because a near/far test is only
as good as the far pairs. Inside a cluster the three sentences are:
.a  the anchor
.b  a LEXICAL paraphrase -- most words shared, one or two swapped.
This is the user's own example ('fishing in the river' vs 'fishing in
the lake'), and it is the EASY half: a bag-of-words model passes it.
.c  a SEMANTIC paraphrase -- same meaning, deliberately few shared words.
This is the half that actually requires an embedding model, and it is
where a broken pooling or a wrong arch shows up first.
So .a-.b and .a-.c are both NEAR pairs but they fail for different reasons,
and the checker reports them separately rather than averaging them away.
There is deliberately NO hand-picked list of hard negatives. The checker
DERIVES them: it ranks every far pair by word overlap and reports the worst
offenders, so the adversarial cases come out of the corpus instead of out of
the author's imagination, and cannot be quietly tuned to pass.
Sentences are 80-95 characters. Long enough to carry a topic, short enough
that seq 64 never truncates (~20 tokens), so this corpus never trips
tasks/0110's truncation refusal and never measures the tokenizer's edges --
reference/corpus.py exists for that and is a different job.
